newsitem.title: UK: Church of England urges discussing gays issue.
newsitem.headline: Church of England urges discussing gays issue.

text.p: The governing body of the Church of England on Monday rejected amendments that would have hardened the church's line on homosexuality and called for more discussion on the subject.
The majority of delegates at the General Synod supported a motion calling for more discussion on the church's position, which accepts homosexual relationships in the laity but not in the clergy.
Hymn-singing gay activists outside the synod welcomed the decision and brandished a banner saying "One small step forward".
Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, the spiritual leader of the church whose head is Queen Elizabeth, made clear in a speech that the church was very far from accepting actively homosexual clergy.

"I do not find any justification, from the Bible or the entire Christian tradition, for sexual activity outside marriage. Thus, same sex relationships in my view cannot be on a par with marriage," Carey said.
Although the decision was welcomed by gay activists, some bishops pointed out that discussion could also lead to a hardening of the present position.

The Reverend Richard Kirker, general secretary of the Lesbian and Gay Christian Movement, said: "We feel it is a good result. The fact that people did not vote for the proposed amendments shows they do not agree with Carey."
The issue has sharply divided the Church of England and this was reflected in the debate, which included speeches by two openly gay priests.

Several members of the clergy said if sexually active gay priests were openly welcomed into the church the clergy and lay people who would leave would far outnumber those who left after a 1992 synod decision to ordain women priests.
